The Vatican says that Pope Leo has lung cancer and that doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung today in a surgery that lasted roughly 90 minutes.

That's the most common type of lung cancer.

It was a localized form of lung cancer.
That means presumably it hasn't spread to other parts of the body.
We don't know that definitively, but presumably that's what that means.

We know before it was removed, it was a nodule.
By definition, a nodule is three centimeters in size or less.
A mass would be greater than three centimeters.

Is removing an affected portion of the lung, Is that curative, or would someone with this diagnosis typically need treatment,
Such as radiation or chemotherapy?

Has it spread to other parts of the body?
That's going to be important because that would be an ominous sign.

Some features can increase the risk of recurrence.

And that will be given once the pathology report is seen.
